issues.description:
Research-only gate before further planning or implementation under cba. Determine what is achievable with existing Dispatcharr plugin APIs, authentication, streaming proxy and the existing Multiview plugin; recommend a supported approach and identify required upstream changes. Do not implement software, deploy services, alter provider settings or create the delivery backlog as part of this task.

Confirmed requirements: all composed playback passes through Dispatcharr, including remote viewers; investigate controls through the same existing public endpoint without direct sidecar access. Sources are Dispatcharr API accounts or Dispatcharr-provided M3U/XC only. Initial experience is 2-4 panels, presets and adjustable split ratios, per-panel channel switching, and audio following panel focus. Media work belongs in a minimal container with Intel VAAPI, Intel QSV, NVIDIA and AMD VAAPI acceleration. Reuse the active Aerio account and permissions with minimal host/port setup and automatic scoped credential provisioning.

Research areas:
1. Compare deployed Dispatcharr capabilities with version-pinned upstream source. Inspect documented plugin lifecycle, actions, custom route support, request identity propagation and internal APIs. Distinguish supported extension points from monkey-patching. Determine whether ordinary viewers need an upstream API extension; current upstream plugin POST actions appear admin-only and do not explicitly pass request identity to run_action.
2. Inspect existing swvn-dispatch/dispatcharr-multiview implementation and license: reuse/extension/collaboration options, channel registration, session ownership, live controls, output transport, audio, dependency footprint and sidecar extraction. Its reviewed README describes PyAV/numpy composition and libx264 with hardware encoding forthcoming; verify against pinned code rather than assuming feature availability.
3. Trace authorization for Dispatcharr API, XC and M3U credentials, including profile restrictions and playlists without verifiable identity. Define feasible client/plugin/sidecar trust boundaries, automatic bootstrap, scoped grants, expiry, rotation, revocation and account changes without asking viewers for admin credentials. Explain any limitations to IP/port-only provisioning.
4. Determine how private per-viewer composites can be relayed and authorized through Dispatcharr, without internal URL leakage, redirects to the sidecar, cross-viewer stream sharing, recursive composite inputs or global lineup pollution. Cover TS/HLS implications, session cleanup, restart and remote control routing.
5. Assess FFmpeg or equivalent pipelines for hardware decode, scale/compose and encode separately across all four required backends. Evaluate channel/layout/audio update mechanisms, continuity, buffering, failure isolation, temporary stream overlap, container variants and host driver requirements. Identify hardware and device experiments needed later; do not present unmeasured performance as verified.
6. Assess upstream connection/session accounting, CPU/GPU/memory/bitrate limits and effects on other viewers. Define the evidence needed to validate 2-4 inputs and focus-following audio on Roku 3820RW2.

References: https://dispatcharr.github.io/Dispatcharr-Docs/plugin-listing/ ; https://github.com/Dispatcharr/Plugins/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md ; https://github.com/Dispatcharr/Dispatcharr/blob/main/Plugins.md ; https://github.com/swvn-dispatch/dispatcharr-multiview ; docs/MULTIVIEW-SIDECAR-SCOPE.md. Registry contribution guidance concerns stable distribution, not development. Reconcile the earlier direct-client pairing proposal with the plugin-mediated design rather than assuming either is already supported.
issues.notes:
Source research completed 2026-09-26 UTC; report: docs/MULTIVIEW-SIDECAR-RESEARCH.md. Pending PO review before closure or further planning. Pins: Dispatcharr v0.31.0 bcbb68c4f054ee56383a41604cfcd7302b85da66 and main e3b482c36be69b5b9778338b239d6c0dcc08d643 (no differences in inspected integration/auth/proxy files); Multiview v0.4.3/main 8e588c67d52ba3c62afffcabfe9112d583647921; FFmpeg 8864fd0aecf21fe9e3cfcd83a8ef33cb7e885fd4. Findings: existing plugin already has NVENC/QSV/VAAPI encoder builders despite stale README, but CPU decode/composition and shared layouts; worker commands only reconnect inputs, no live channel/geometry/audio switching. Core plugin POST actions are admin-only with no caller in action context. Plain M3U can be anonymous; XC/API can supply identity. Existing plugin internal inputs use user=None and dashboard auth lacks viewer ownership, so cannot be reused as the authorization boundary. Private media relay needs explicit session authorization; normal live proxy is AllowAny/network-gated. Stream-limit policy may evict existing playback, requiring reserve-or-reject admission. Recommend narrow upstream viewer/session/relay extension plus lightweight plugin and GPU sidecar; externally routed plugin listener is a configuration-heavy alternative. PO decisions: integration path, anonymous M3U enrollment/account requirement, and whether declared hybrid CPU composition is acceptable. All hardware/device/latency tests remain unexecuted; report includes concrete validation matrix. No software implementation, service deployment, upstream contact or additional beads.
PO requested a written plan following the research. Added local docs/MULTIVIEW-DELIVERY-PLAN.md: proposed responsibilities, six delivery phases and exit gates, explicit upstream requirements (viewer extension API, identity/channel authorization, private playback relay, non-evicting input admission and lifecycle/compatibility), pending product decisions, and a draft maintainer proposal. No further beads or upstream contact; research/plan pending PO review.

issues.description:
GitHub #10 (OPEN as of 2026-10-01): https://github.com/EndofLineTech/AerioTV-Roku/issues/10

### AerioTV release

0.3.86

### Roku model and OS version

Streaming Stick+ 3810X, Roku OS 15.3

### Connection type

Dispatcharr

### Dispatcharr version (if applicable)

0.31.0

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start playback
2. Press back - this goes back to the guide view
3. Press back - this goes back to playback

### Expected behavior

There should be an easy way to stop playback.

### Actual behavior

The only way to stop playback of the current channel is to play another channel or press OK, then hold OK, arrow up then right 5 times. That is 7 key presses for something that should be pretty easy to do.

### Photos or additional details

_No response_

Triage: reported against AerioTV 0.3.86; reproduce before implementing.

Native 3820RW2 local candidate: tuned authorized live channel until ECP media-player play, Back minimized, Play expanded, Back minimized, Back stopped; read-only ECP media-player reported close/error=false and mini-player disappeared from guide. Developer screenshots cannot prove picture/sound. npm run verify passed; original 0.3.87 app restored. Source remains local/unpublished; await PO acceptance/release integration.

comments.author: MotWakorb
comments.text:
DEFERRED DEVICE ACCEPTANCE — PO is remote and cannot test now. Resume physical-remote acceptance when PO has access; do not treat lack of results as a failure or close stories from model tests alone. Current installed build: 0.2.7, 3820RW2, OS 15.3.4 build 2402, Dispatcharr 0.31.0. ECP remains Limited.

Already verified: eight off-device suites, compiler/package build, developer installation, native launch, and admin capability refresh. Playback/navigation additions below are NOT hardware-accepted yet.

Deferred test record:
1. Baseline playback: tune representative channels; confirm picture/audio, pause/resume, audio/subtitle selection, caption mode, and recovery after an unavailable stream. Confirm no regressions from 0.2.6.
2. Direction and rapid tuning (ihp.1/.7/.8): Up next/Down previous by default; change direction preference and relaunch; verify guide-filter order, endpoints, held/rapid presses, cancelled previews and no unintended tunes while navigating overlays.
3. Recent/previous persistence (ihp.2/.3/.5, b17.1): watch A then B; Right alternates A/B after successful playback; Replay shows ordered deduplicated recents with logos/now titles. Preview-only and failed tunes must not count as watched. Verify empty/removed entries, 25-entry bound, relaunch persistence, server/account isolation, legacy preference migration and save-failure notice.
4. Channels browser (ihp.4): Left opens over ongoing playback; Watching badge and now titles match; group selection stays local to overlay; OK tunes; nested Back restores correct focus. Test long/empty groups and responsiveness with the 1,335-channel lineup.
5. Mini-player and Back ladder (ihp.6/.7): dismiss options/info before minimizing; video/audio continue in guide; guide remains readable and navigable. Back or OK on playing channel expands without reconnecting. Explicit Stop closes playback. Test rapid Back, options-open cases, tuning another channel, setup/account edits and playback errors while minimized. Compare Dispatcharr client identities/counts before/after repeated minimize/expand and Stop.
6. Transport (ihp.8): OK recalls info without pausing; Down enters controls; arrows stay in controls; Play/Pause, Channels, Recent, Minimize, Options and Stop work and restore focus correctly. Schedule progress must not imply a seekable rewind buffer.
7. Sleep timer (ihp.9): 30/60/90/120-minute choices, remaining-time display and cancellation; retain deadline over channel changes and mini-player; Stop/app exit clears timer. Verify native expiry stops once, including paused/minimized playback. Deterministic expiry/cancellation model tests already pass; any shortened device-test duration must be temporary and documented.
8. Stream Info (ihp.11): compare native codec/audio/bitrate/buffering facts on representative streams; absent metrics explicitly Unavailable; retuning must not show prior-channel facts; no credentials/provider URLs. Capture decoder-stat schema and establish resolution/frame-rate semantics before mapping those metrics.
9. Source switching (ihp.12, ah5.4): admin list shows valid member sources and active/reported-active distinction; choose/confirm a source and verify actual upstream changes while the same Roku client stays connected. Include another viewer and compare client identities/counts, not counts alone. Test cancel, delayed result after menu close/retune, revoked permissions, restricted account, offline/error/timeout, stale membership and unconfirmed change. Shared-viewer effect must be readable before confirmation.
10. Persistence/capability integration (b17.1, ah5.4): actual registry save/relaunch and account changes; capability refresh remains scoped to current account, unknown/denied permissions recover honestly, old Task responses cannot overwrite a new session.
11. Visual/performance acceptance: readable focus and long labels, logos, now-airing text, mini-player bounds, transport and options at 1080p; program-boundary metadata refresh; responsive browsing and sustained playback on large lineup. Capture screenshots where useful; black screenshot video plane is not picture/audio proof.

Separate unfinished feasibility work, not testable shipped controls: ihp.10 Fit/Fill/Stretch needs a proven native mapping and 4:3/16:9/letterboxed-source tests across fullscreen/mini before exposing choices. ihp.13 audio-only needs PO scope decision plus foreground/lifecycle/screensaver/TV-off feasibility evidence; no background-playback promise or audio-only control is present.

When testing resumes, record build, channel/codec, exact remote sequence, observed vs expected behavior, redacted native logs and server-session evidence on the corresponding story. Close only stories whose acceptance is satisfied; obtain PO acceptance before closing the epic. Reference documentation: docs/PLAYER-CONTRACT.md and docs/DEVICE-VALIDATION.md.
